findings.title: Used backup code slots set to null can be matched if backupCode is not a string or via external Totp flow
findings.body: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` lines 113-129, third-party identity provider (Google/SAML) users with 2FA enabled are only exempted from `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` and password checks when `credentials.totpCode` is truthy (`!credentials.totpCode`). When such a user loses access to their authenticator and tries to log in using a `backupCode` (where `credentials.totpCode` is empty), `authorize` throws `ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` at line 114 before reaching the backup code check at line 131. Furthermore, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` line 180, when `totpEmail` is set (the 2FA step after SSO login), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, so the "Lost access" button to enter a backup code is never even shown to SSO users.

findings.title: Unvalidated `req.body.backupCode` allows bypassing 2FA disable check once a backup code has been used
findings.body: When a backup code is used during login (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` line 148), the consumed entry in the `backupCodes` array is replaced with `null` (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and re-encrypted. In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, `req.body` is not validated with a schema before use. If a caller sends a JSON body with a truthy non-string `backupCode` or if `req.body.backupCode` is not type-checked, or more importantly if `replaceAll` is called on a non-string it throws, while if someone crafts `backupCodes.indexOf(...)`, note that in `disable.ts` line 61 `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` only produces a string, so `indexOf` won't match `null` directly—however, if `req.body.backupCode` is not a string (e.g. an object/array/boolean), `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws an unhandled `TypeError` resulting in a 500 response instead of a 400.

findings.title: Closing the modal on the backup codes step via backdrop/Escape leaves UI out of sync with enabled 2FA
findings.body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, 2FA is already enabled on the server when `handleEnable` succeeds (line 134), which transitions the modal to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` without calling `onEnable()` yet. `onEnable()` and `resetState()` are only invoked when the user clicks the explicit "Close" button (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`, line 266). If the user dismisses the dialog via the `X` close button, pressing Escape, or clicking the overlay (which triggers `Dialog`'s `onOpenChange`), `onEnable()` is never called so the parent settings page still shows 2FA as disabled, and `resetState()` is never called so reopening the modal starts on the backup codes step instead of resetting.

findings.title: Passing `type="password"` to `PasswordField` overrides the show/hide password toggle
findings.body: In `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` lines 36-39, `PasswordField` sets `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` BEFORE spreading `{...props}` onto `InputField`. In `apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` line 176, `PasswordField` is rendered with `type="password"`, which overwrites the computed `type` prop and makes the eye toggle button unable to reveal the password.
